description: analyse.py --force-thread comm=CrRendererMain over run 1's banked sample stream (no browser launched)

requiredRecord.reason: controls did not behave on the selected thread

actual.reason: no thread with comm='CrRendererMain' in any sample

note: Same finding as R-B, for the renderer's main thread: the comm recorded for it is 'chrome', not 'CrRendererMain', on this Chrome build/machine. See redcase-R-B.json for the full explanation (one exhaustive scan covered both). The protocol's own text pre-registers that R-C might not be caught even if the thread were found ('it may not be, because the renderer main thread does real work...'); what actually happened is a step earlier than that: the named thread was never found by comm at all, so the busy predicate was never reached for either R-B or R-C. No threshold was tightened or loosened in response; no substitute thread-selection mechanism (e.g. tid==pid) was added.
